registrations.name: driver_defer_action
registrations.description:
PRE-SCHEDULE driver tool calls to execute THE INSTANT a kernel module loads or a process starts. This solves the critical timing problem: many drivers (EAC, BattlEye, Vanguard) wipe their IAT, decrypt code, or perform anti-RE operations during initialization. By the time you can manually react, the evidence is already destroyed. This tool lets you queue actions (read memory, set HW breakpoints, dump module, etc.) that fire IMMEDIATELY when the target appears - before its init routine runs. 

Template parameters in action params are resolved at trigger time:
  ${module_base} - runtime kernel base address of the loaded module
  ${module_size} - module image size
  ${module_name} - resolved module filename
  ${pid} - process ID (for process_start)
  ${base_address} - process image base (for process_start)

Address arithmetic: '${module_base}+0x17C000' computes base+offset automatically.

Example: to capture EAC's IAT before it's wiped:
  wait_for='kernel_module_load', target='EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys',
  actions=[{tool:'driver_read_kernel_memory', params:{address:'${module_base}+0x17C000', size:64}}]

parameters.description: Condition type: 'kernel_module_load' or 'process_start'

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Module or process name to watch for (case-insensitive substring match). E.g. 'EasyAntiCheat_EOS.sys', 'BEService.exe'

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: Array of tool calls to execute when condition is met. Each entry: {"tool": "tool_name", "params": {...}}. Compatibility aliases accepted: top-level {action, params} and per-entry {action, params}. Params may use ${module_base}, ${module_size}, ${pid}, ${base_address} templates.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the condition (default 300 = 5 minutes)

parameters.name: poll_interval
parameters.description: Milliseconds between condition checks (default 50ms). Lower = faster reaction but more CPU. For IAT capture, use 10-25ms.

parameters.name: binary_id
parameters.description: Optional session id to target (returned by `sessions_manage` action=list). When omitted the active session is used.

registrations.name: driver_sniff_network_buffers
registrations.description:
Manage a kernel-level network buffer sniff session that works with hardware breakpoints to capture plaintext network buffers in memory BEFORE encryption. Wireshark only sees encrypted payloads; this tool captures the data before it reaches ws2_32.dll!send, afd.sys!AfdFastIoDeviceControl, or a custom game/malware encryption function.

Workflow:
1. Call with address + buffer_register + size_register to START session
2. Set HW breakpoint on the address via driver_set_hw_breakpoint
3. When BP fires, read thread context, read buffer from memory, call with operation='store'
4. Call with operation='get' to retrieve all captured buffers
5. Call with operation='stop' when done

This is a composite tool that coordinates with driver_set_hw_breakpoint and read_memory.

parameters.description: Alias for bytes when operation='store'

registrations.description: Enter PLAN mode. Use this when the user's request would benefit from planning before implementation. Plan mode is read-only: edit/write/bash and other mutation tools become hard-denied. Once a plan is ready, call plan_exit to switch to the build agent. Call this tool when: the user explicitly asks for a plan; the request is complex enough to benefit from research and design first; the task involves multiple files or architectural decisions.
